_doc: Curated beneficial / protective species list. Match is exact on species name. Drilldown badges fire on BOTH the increased-list (rising beneficial = favorable) AND the decreased-list (falling beneficial = caution). Conservative; absence here means 'not on our list,' not 'neutral.'

Streptococcus salivarius.note: Oral commensal; certain strains (e.g., K12) reduce upper respiratory infection rates in clinical trials.

Lactobacillus salivarius.note: Oral and gut commensal; documented probiotic and immunomodulatory effects.
Lactobacillus salivarius.ref: Messaoudi et al., Microb Cell Fact 2013

Lactobacillus crispatus.note: Mucosal commensal associated with low pH and exclusion of pathogens.

Lactobacillus rhamnosus.note: Common probiotic strain with documented immunomodulatory and barrier-supporting effects.
Lactobacillus rhamnosus.ref: Sanders et al., Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019

Dolosigranulum pigrum.note: Nasal commensal; abundance inversely associated with respiratory infection in cohort studies.
Dolosigranulum pigrum.ref: Biesbroek et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2014

Corynebacterium accolens.note: Nasal commensal; produces free fatty acids that suppress S. pneumoniae growth in culture.

Staphylococcus epidermidis.note: Skin commensal; produces antimicrobial peptides active against S. aureus and supports barrier function.
Staphylococcus epidermidis.ref: Cogen et al., J Invest Dermatol 2010

Staphylococcus hominis.note: Skin commensal; certain strains produce lantibiotics that inhibit S. aureus.
Staphylococcus hominis.ref: Nakatsuji et al., Sci Transl Med 2017

Roseomonas mucosa.note: Skin commensal; topical application improved atopic dermatitis in early trials.

Cutibacterium acnes.note: Predominant skin commensal in sebaceous areas; helps maintain low skin pH and crowds out transient pathogens.

Bifidobacterium longum.note: Gut commensal; immunomodulatory and frequent probiotic constituent.
Bifidobacterium longum.ref: Sanders et al., Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019

Bifidobacterium breve.note: Gut commensal; supports mucosal barrier and immune development.
Bifidobacterium breve.ref: Sanders et al., Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019

Akkermansia muciniphila.note: Mucin-degrading gut commensal; lower abundance associated with metabolic disease.
Akkermansia muciniphila.ref: Cani et al., Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol 2022

Faecalibacterium prausnitzii.note: Major butyrate-producing gut commensal; reduced abundance associated with IBD.

Bacteroides fragilis.note: Gut commensal; capsular polysaccharide A drives regulatory T-cell development in mouse models.

Roseburia intestinalis.note: Butyrate producer in the gut; associated with anti-inflammatory effects.
